ENFORCEMENT RULE OF THE ACT ON THE PREVENTION AND MANAGEMENT OF CARDIO-CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASES

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Rule is to prescribe matters delegated by the Act on the Prevention and Management of Cardio-Cerebrovascular Diseases and its Enforcement Decree, and matters necessary for their implementation.

Article 2 Deleted. <June 22, 2023>

Article 3 Deleted. <June 22, 2023>

Article 4 (Research Advisory Group on Cardio-Cerebrovascular Diseases)
① The Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency may operate a research advisory group on cardio-cerebrovascular diseases (hereinafter referred to as the "research advisory group"), composed of experts in that field, to provide expert advice on the cardio-cerebrovascular disease research projects under Article 8 (2) 1, 5, and 6 of the Act on the Prevention and Management of Cardio-Cerebrovascular Diseases (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"). <Amended on September 11, 2020 and June 22, 2023>
② The Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency shall designate the head of the research advisory group from among its members and commission its members from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience in the field of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases. <Amended on September 11, 2020>
③ Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the research advisory group, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① and ②, shall be determined by the Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency. <Amended on September 11, 2020>

Article 5 (Cardio-Cerebrovascular Disease Survey and Statistics Projects)
① Where the Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency considers it necessary for the prevention and management of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases, the Commissioner may disclose the results of the cardio-cerebrovascular disease survey and statistics projects under Article 9 (1) of the Act (hereinafter referred to as "cardio-cerebrovascular disease survey and statistics projects"), as determined by the Commissioner. <Amended on September 11, 2020 and June 22, 2023>
② When requesting the submission of materials, the presentation of opinions, or other assistance necessary for cardio-cerebrovascular disease survey and statistics projects under Article 9 (3) of the Act, the Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency shall make the request in writing, specifying the purpose, duration, and method of use and other relevant matters. <Amended on September 11, 2020 and June 22, 2023>

Article 6 (Criteria and Procedures for Designation of the Central Cardio-Cerebrovascular Disease Center)
① The criteria for designation of the central cardio-cerebrovascular disease center under Article 12 (1) of the Act shall be as set out in Annex 1. <Amended on June 22, 2023>
② A person seeking designation as the central cardio-cerebrovascular disease center shall submit to the Minister of Health and Welfare an application in attached Form No. 1, accompanied by the following documents: <Amended on June 22, 2023>
1. Documents proving compliance with the designation criteria in Annex 1.
2. Current status of personnel deployment.
3. Operational plan.
③ The Minister of Health and Welfare shall designate the central cardio-cerebrovascular disease center following deliberation by the Cardio-Cerebrovascular Disease Management Committee under Article 5 of the Act (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee"). In such cases, the Minister shall issue a certificate of designation in attached Form No. 2 to the designated central center. <Amended on June 22, 2023>
④ As determined by the Minister of Health and Welfare, the head of the central center shall report annually to the Minister on its operational plan, progress of activities, financial management plan, details of financial expenditure, and other relevant matters. <Amended on June 22, 2023>
⑤ Matters necessary for designation of the central center, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ④, shall be determined by the Minister of Health and Welfare. <Amended on June 22, 2023>

Article 7 (Criteria and Procedures for Designation of Regional Cardio-Cerebrovascular Disease Centers)
① The criteria for designation of regional cardio-cerebrovascular disease centers under Article 13 (1) of the Act shall be as set out in Annex 2.
② A person seeking designation as a regional center shall submit to the Minister of Health and Welfare an application in attached Form No. 3, accompanied by the following documents:
1. Documents proving compliance with the designation criteria in Annex 2.
2. Current status of personnel deployment.
3. Operational plan.
③ When the Minister of Health and Welfare designates a regional center, the Minister shall issue a certificate of designation in attached Form No. 4.
④ Notwithstanding paragraph ①, where designation of a regional center is necessary in light of local circumstances, the Minister of Health and Welfare may, following deliberation by the Committee, designate a person who does not meet the criteria in paragraph ① as the regional center for that area.
⑤ Detailed matters necessary for designation of regional centers, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ④, shall be determined by the Minister of Health and Welfare.

Article 8 (Criteria and Procedures for Designation of Local Cardio-Cerebrovascular Disease Centers)
① The criteria for designation of local cardio-cerebrovascular disease centers under Article 13 (1) of the Act shall be as follows:
1. The center shall be an emergency medical institution designated under the Emergency Medical Service Act and shall maintain a 24-hour response system for cardiovascular or cerebrovascular diseases.
2. The center shall participate in the project for establishing a cardio-cerebrovascular disease care delivery system implemented by the Minister of Health and Welfare.
3. The center shall maintain a cooperative system with a regional center designated under Article 7.
4. The center shall have physicians whose experience in surgery or interventional procedures has been certified by professional medical societies related to cardiovascular or cerebrovascular diseases.
② The Minister of Health and Welfare may designate local cardio-cerebrovascular disease centers separately as local cardiovascular disease centers and local cerebrovascular disease centers. In such cases, the designation types may be integrated, surgical, or interventional procedure types.
③ A person seeking designation as a local center shall submit to the Minister of Health and Welfare an application in attached Form No. 5, accompanied by documents proving compliance with the designation criteria in each subparagraph of paragraph ①.
④ When the Minister of Health and Welfare designates a local center, the Minister shall issue a certificate of designation in attached Form No. 6.
⑤ Where necessary to carry out the activities in each subparagraph of Article 13 (1) of the Act, a local center may carry out such activities in cooperation with regional centers, other local centers, public health centers with jurisdiction, and other relevant institutions.
⑥ Detailed matters necessary for designation of local centers, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ⑤, shall be determined by the Minister of Health and Welfare.

Article 9 (Methods of Evaluation and Redesignation of Regional and Local Cardio-Cerebrovascular Disease Centers)
① Evaluation of regional and local centers under Article 13 (2) of the Act shall be conducted separately as documentary evaluation and on-site evaluation.
② Documentary evaluation under paragraph ① shall be conducted annually for all regional and local centers; on-site evaluation shall be conducted where verification of documentary evaluation results is necessary.
③ The Minister of Health and Welfare may request a specialized institution, such as the Health Insurance Review and Assessment Service under Article 62 of the National Health Insurance Act, to carry out work relating to evaluation for redesignation of regional and local centers.
④ Institutions designated as regional or local centers shall submit annually the materials necessary for evaluation and redesignation under Article 15 (1) of the Act.
⑤ Based on the results of three years of evaluations under paragraphs ① through ③, the Minister of Health and Welfare shall determine whether to redesignate the relevant regional or local center following deliberation by the Committee and shall issue a new designation certificate to a redesignated institution.
⑥ Detailed methods of evaluation of regional and local centers, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ⑤, shall be determined by the Minister of Health and Welfare.

Article 10 (Procedures for Revocation of Designation of Regional or Local Cardio-Cerebrovascular Disease Centers)
① When intending to revoke a designation under Article 13 (5) of the Act, the Minister of Health and Welfare shall notify the head of the regional or local center, specifying the grounds.
② Where a regional or local center fails to obtain redesignation under Article 13 (3) of the Act or its designation is revoked under Article 13 (5) of the Act, it shall not display signs or other indications identifying it as a regional or local cardio-cerebrovascular disease center.

Article 11 (Establishment and Operation of the Cardio-Cerebrovascular Disease Information System)
① The Minister of Health and Welfare and the Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency may handle the following duties through the cardio-cerebrovascular disease information system under Article 14 (1) of the Act:
1. Collection and analysis of data necessary for cardio-cerebrovascular disease research projects under Article 8 (1) of the Act.
2. Collection and analysis of data necessary for cardio-cerebrovascular disease survey and statistics projects under Article 9 (1) of the Act.
3. Collection and analysis of data necessary for cardio-cerebrovascular disease prevention projects under Article 10 (1) of the Act.
4. Other duties that the Minister of Health and Welfare or the Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency considers necessary for the efficient performance of work relating to cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.
② Matters necessary for establishing and operating the information system, other than those prescribed in paragraph ①, shall be determined by the Minister of Health and Welfare.

Article 12 (Requests for Submission of Materials)
When requesting the submission of materials or the presentation of opinions under Article 15 (1) of the Act, the Minister of Health and Welfare, the Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, the Special Metropolitan City Mayor, a Metropolitan City Mayor, a Special Self-Governing City Mayor, a Do Governor, or a Special Self-Governing Province Governor (hereinafter referred to as a "Mayor/Do Governor"), or the head of a Si (city), Gun (county), or Gu (district), including persons to whom authority has been delegated or entrusted under Article 20 of the Act, shall make the request in writing, specifying the purpose, period, and method of use and other relevant matters.

Article 13 (Measures to Ensure the Security of Personal Information)
① The Minister of Health and Welfare, the Commissioner of the Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency, a Mayor/Do Governor, or the head of a Si (city), Gun (county), or Gu (district), including persons to whom authority has been delegated or entrusted under Article 20 of the Act, shall take the following measures necessary to ensure the security of personal information under Article 15 (3) of the Act:
1. Formulation and implementation of a management plan for secure processing of personal information.
2. Control of access to personal information and restriction of access privileges.
3. Installation and updating of security programs for personal information.
4. Application of encryption technology or equivalent measures for secure storage and transmission of personal information.
5. Retention of access logs to respond to personal information breaches and measures to prevent their forgery or alteration.
6. Physical measures, such as installation of locking devices, for secure storage of personal information.
② Detailed standards for the security measures under paragraph ① shall be determined by the Minister of Health and Welfare.

Article 14 (Review of Regulations)
The Minister of Health and Welfare shall review the appropriateness of the criteria and procedures for designation of central, regional, and local cardio-cerebrovascular disease centers under Articles 6 through 8 every three years from July 1, 2023, meaning before July 1 of every third year, and take measures for improvement or other necessary action. <Amended on June 22, 2023>

CRITERIA FOR DESIGNATION OF THE CENTRAL CARDIO-CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE CENTER
Annex 1 to the Enforcement Rule of the Act on the Prevention and Management of Cardio-Cerebrovascular Diseases <Newly inserted on June 22, 2023>
(Relating to Article 6 (1))

1. General criteria
(a) The center shall have the clinical and research capabilities necessary to play a leading role in national cardio-cerebrovascular disease management.
(b) The center shall have the facilities, equipment, and personnel necessary to provide education and training for persons engaged in cardio-cerebrovascular disease management.
(c) The center shall have personnel capable of evaluating regional and local cardio-cerebrovascular disease centers.
(d) The center shall have specialist personnel and equipment for registration projects, surveys, and research relating to cardio-cerebrovascular disease management.
(e) The center shall have specialist personnel and equipment capable of supporting national statistical data and policy projects concerning cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.

2. Organizational operation criteria
(a) A director and a deputy director of the central cardio-cerebrovascular disease center shall be appointed to perform the duties under Article 12 (1) of the Act.
(b) The director shall be appointed, in consultation with the Minister of Health and Welfare, from among medical personnel under the Medical Service Act who have at least ten years of experience in clinical practice, research, or policy support in the field of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.
(c) The director's term shall be at least two years, and professional expertise and independence in the performance of duties shall be guaranteed.
(d) The central center shall be organized and operated independently, separately from other organizational structures.
(e) Separate teams shall be established and operated for building a nationwide cooperative system for cardio-cerebrovascular disease management; supporting the operation and evaluation of regional and local centers; conducting research on cardio-cerebrovascular diseases; and providing preventive education and publicity concerning cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.

CRITERIA FOR DESIGNATION OF REGIONAL CARDIO-CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE CENTERS
Annex 2 to the Enforcement Rule of the Act on the Prevention and Management of Cardio-Cerebrovascular Diseases <Newly inserted on June 22, 2023>
(Relating to Article 7 (1))

1. General criteria
(a) A comprehensive medical and surgical care system covering the full range of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases shall be established.
(b) As a regional emergency medical center designated under the Emergency Medical Service Act, the center shall maintain a 24-hour response system for severe and emergency cardio-cerebrovascular diseases.
(c) A management system covering the entire continuum, including prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation of patients with cardio-cerebrovascular diseases, shall be established.
(d) A cooperative system for cardio-cerebrovascular diseases involving the area served, local medical institutions, local medical associations, and other relevant parties shall be established.
(e) The organization and personnel necessary to implement comprehensive care and management throughout the entire continuum of cardio-cerebrovascular diseases shall be secured on a stable basis.

2. Essential facility and personnel criteria
(a) The center shall have a cardiovascular intensive care unit, a neurological intensive care unit, a cardio-cerebrovascular angiography room, a stroke intensive treatment unit, and an operating room.
(b) Specialists for triage and initial response for emergency cardio-cerebrovascular patients shall be secured.
(c) Specialists in cardiovascular interventional procedures and cerebrovascular interventional procedures shall be secured.
(d) Specialists in cardiac surgery and brain surgery shall be secured.
(e) Educational facilities for cardio-cerebrovascular disease prevention and management and facilities for rehabilitation treatment shall be secured.
(f) Specialists for cardio-cerebrovascular disease prevention and management and rehabilitation treatment shall be secured.
(g) Office space for the operation of the regional center's activities shall be secured.
(h) Personnel responsible for patient registration management, nurses dedicated to education, center operations managers, and administrative personnel shall be secured.

3. Treatment capability criteria
(a) Number of coronary interventions and proportions performed at night, on public holidays, and in emergencies.
(b) Combined number of coronary artery bypass operations, aortic operations, and valve operations.
(c) Number of extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) procedures.
(d) Number of cerebrovascular interventions and proportions performed at night, on public holidays, and in emergencies.
(e) Number of intravenous thrombolysis procedures and proportion performed in emergencies.
(f) Number of craniotomies.

Note:
Compliance with the treatment capability criteria shall be assessed by comprehensively considering the quantitative levels of the indicators in each item and qualitative levels, including clinical performance capability.
